introduction: Explore the science behind how your body and brain process different sensations like touch, pain, te

vocabulary.definition: a neurological condition in which certain signals from the nervous system are interrupted or impaired
vocabulary.example: Ian Waterman was diagnosed with deafferentation, causing him to lose all sensation from the neck down.

vocabulary.definition: the awareness of the position and movement of the body
vocabulary.example: Proprioception is essential for balance and coordination, allowing us to move without constantly looking at our limbs.

vocabulary.definition: cells that sense mechanical deformation of the skin
vocabulary.example: Mechanoreceptors in the skin help us feel touch, pressure, and vibrations.

vocabulary.definition: cells that respond to changes in temperature
vocabulary.example: When exposed to extreme heat, thermoreceptors signal the brain to perceive the sensation of burning.

vocabulary.definition: nerve cells that respond to harmful stimuli, such as pain
vocabulary.example: Nociceptors are responsible for the sensation of pain when you injure yourself.

vocabulary.definition: relating to the sense of touch
vocabulary.example: Rubbing an injured area provides tactile feedback, temporarily relieving pain.
